items.detail:
3 findings carried by reviewers against `data/reviews/evidence/verify-daybreak-defense-network-product-wording.md`, batched into one job because they concern the same file. Each is stated below in the reviewing reviewer's own words. Fix every one, or say in `RESULT.md` which you did not and why — a finding you leave standing must keep its file.

### "inside a single second" is wrong for the 22:53 run — say "within seconds"

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-1.md`.

The narrative says "In each of the two runs made inside a single second the spread is under ten bytes", but the transcript appended in the same diff timestamps the 22:53 run 04:52:58.726Z → 04:53:03.981Z — 5.3 seconds, not one. The substance holds (spread 5 bytes), only the descriptor is wrong; "within seconds" or "inside six seconds" fixes it. Worth correcting because this job exists to stop a measurement being described at the wrong timescale.

### The 20:32 row's two counts came from two different header sets, and the table does not say so

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-2.md`.

The new table lists "20:32 | 376,021 / 376,069" as one run, but the blockquote immediately above it records that 376,021 was the UA-only fetch and 376,069 the UA + accept-language + cache-control fetch. The sentence "Not monotonically — 20:32's 376,069 sits above the whole 21:36 run" therefore rests on the one measurement in the whole table taken with `cache-control: no-cache`. Adding "(different header sets — see the blockquote)" to that row would keep the confound visible; nothing in the conclusion changes, since the sentence it supports is a hedge.

### A fifth run 17 minutes later breaks the rising-floor pattern

Carried in `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-3.md`.

This review re-fetched the URL at 23:10 local (UA only) and got 376,100 / 376,116 / 376,108 — a floor of 376,100, below the 22:53 run's 376,108. "each run's floor is higher than the last" is exactly true of the four rows tabulated and is not overstated as a law, but a reader may take it as a trend; a half-clause noting the floors are only monotonic at hours-apart spacing would close that reading. Nothing in the argument depends on it — the 105-byte gap the record set out to explain is still far outside the seconds-scale band.

### Retiring these findings

These files' presence is what puts the findings in the Pulse's derived queue. Delete the file for each finding you fixed, in the same diff as the fix — that is what removes the item, and a file left in place puts the same finding back on the next Pulse run:

- `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-1.md`
- `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-2.md`
- `data/carried/j-20260904-54-carry-3.md`

items.detail:
The evidence file's header says the raw transcript is a "node fetch+strip+count script, 2026-09-03; the huggingface.co/meta-models org page was fetched twice because its activity feed renders intermittently". Grepping "^=== https" over data/reviews/evidence/verify-meta-spark-weights-pending-status.raw.txt returns 11 fetch blocks and huggingface.co/meta-models appears exactly once (line 22). The underlying observation is real — that page's stripped length was 2556 in the transcript and 2548 when I fetched it myself minutes later — but as written the sentence describes a second fetch the transcript does not contain. Either capture both fetches, or say it plainly ("the page was fetched in both this run and the earlier one and rendered differently; only this run's is captured"). This is the same narrative-outruns-transcript shape the previous pass flagged, at much smaller scale, which is why it is carried rather than blocked on.

## Origin

Transcribed by the loop from the verdict record for job j-20260903-14 (`j-20260903-14.md`), which is the one channel a review has: the reviewer's edits to the tree it reviewed are discarded, so a finding it noticed but did not block on reaches work sources only by being written in its record and copied here.
